Who We Are
Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.
We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation , more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.
You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries.
What You'll Do
Design, build, and maintain scalable distributed backend systems capable of handling high-volume traffic from hundreds of thousands of devices deployed globally.
Develop and optimize backend services, APIs, data models, and infrastructure components to support reliable product functionality across Verkada’s platform.
Design scalable control planes and data primitives for Verkada products, ensuring high availability, performance, security, and maintainability.
Build and deploy new backend services within a microservices architecture, including service design, implementation, testing, monitoring, and production support.
Collaborate with product, infrastructure, firmware, and frontend engineering teams to define technical requirements and deliver backend systems that support customer-facing product features.
Participate in code reviews, technical design discussions, and engineering best practices to ensure high-quality, maintainable software development.
What You Bring
A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a closely related field.
Must be willing and able to work onsite five days per week
US Employee Benefits
Verkada is committed to fostering a workplace environment that prioritizes the holistic health and wellbeing of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive wellness perks, benefits, and resources. Our benefits and perks programs include, but are not limited to:
Healthcare programs that can be tailored to meet the personal health and financial well-being needs - Premiums are 100% covered for the employee under at least one plan and 80% for family premiums under all plans
Nationwide medical, vision and dental coverage
Health Saving Account (HSA) with annual employer contributions and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) with tax saving options
Expanded mental health support
Paid parental leave policy & fertility benefits
Time off to relax and recharge through our paid holidays, firmwide extended holidays, flexible PTO and personal sick time
Professional development stipend
Fertility Stipend
Wellness/fitness benefits
Healthy lunches provided daily
Commuter benefits

You must be independently authorized to work in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa for this role, at this time.

With that in mind, we carefully consider a number of factors to determine the appropriate starting pay for an employee, including their primary work location and an assessment of a candidate's skills and experience, as well as market demands and internal parity. The Cameras team is the cornerstone of Verkada's product ecosystem. We are looking for a Director of Firmware Engineering to lead the embedded software organization behind our flagship camera line. In this role, you will oversee multiple specialized firmware groups, driving the development of highly reliable, performant, and secure firmware deployed to hundreds of thousands of devices worldwide.
You will manage and mentor a team of engineering managers and senior individual contributors, partnering closely with Hardware, Cloud, Product, and QA teams to define the roadmap and deliver cutting-edge edge-computing and imaging capabilities.
What You’ll Do
Partner on New Product Development (NPI): Work side-by-side with the Hardware and Electrical Engineering teams from the conceptual phase through mass production. You will co-design system architectures, evaluate new silicon (SoCs, sensors), provide early firmware requirements for board designs, and ensure seamless hardware-software integration for our next generation of cameras.
Oversee Core Camera Firmware: the group responsible for the foundation of our camera OS. This includes driving new hardware bring-up, porting vendor SDKs, developing low-level drivers, and managing robust Over-The-Air (OTA) firmware update mechanisms.
Oversee Camera Imaging Systems: the team dedicated to maximizing image quality. They guide efforts in Image Signal Processor (ISP) tuning, sensor integration, and optimizing the end-to-end imaging and video encoding pipeline.
Drive Firmware Delivery & Quality: Champion the group responsible for deploying new firmware releases at a massive scale. You will oversee the development of release tooling, refine deployment processes, establish CI/CD best practices, and closely monitor fleet health metrics to ensure exceptional reliability.
Scale and Mentor the Team: Recruit, hire, and mentor exceptional firmware engineers and engineering managers. Foster a culture of technical excellence, continuous learning, and cross-functional collaboration.
What You Bring
BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
8+ years of hands-on embedded software or firmware engineering experience, with a proven track record of shipping high-volume consumer or enterprise hardware products.
4+ years of engineering management experience, including experience managing other managers and leading organizations of 15+ engineers.
Technical expertise with Linux and C for embedded systems.
Experience with ISP tuning and image processing pipelines is highly preferred.
Strong understanding of modern software delivery practices, including CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and fleet-wide release management.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical decisions into business impact for executive stakeholders.
Prefer familiarity with modern camera architectures, and camera SoCs (e.g., Ambarella, Qualcomm, or similar).

We deliver the efficiency required to store petabytes of high-quality video across millions of deployed cameras, making sure every byte is stored reliably and accessible instantly.

About the Team
The Camera Firmware Platform team owns the foundation that every Verkada camera runs on. While our product firmware teams bring new camera categories to market, this team makes every camera in the fleet, both existing and future models, more reliable, faster, leaner, and more power-efficient.
Edge Storage: We own the on-camera storage stack that turns every Verkada camera into a self-contained recording device. Our mandate is reliable, accessible, secure, and observable storage of customer video. Footage is preserved instantly across SD cards and raw NAND, even during network outages or sudden power loss, for millions of cameras and petabytes of video. This extends to the backend services that manage retention, cloud backup, and storage health across the fleet.
Firmware Platform: Building on that foundation, we own the cross-cutting firmware systems underneath every camera feature: boot and shutdown, memory and power management, system state orchestration, IPC, observability, and firmware update. We build these once, for every camera model and SoC, so product teams can move fast without rebuilding the same infrastructure.
About the Role
As the Engineering Manager for Camera Firmware Platform, you will lead a highly technical team of storage and embedded systems engineers responsible for the reliability, performance, power, and stability of firmware running on a fleet of more than 1.8 million perpetually online devices. You will set the storage and platform roadmap, decide which fleet-wide investments matter most, and turn them into measurable improvements in footage retention, storage endurance, boot time, memory headroom, power draw, and crash rates.
You will partner closely with the Camera Firmware product team, Hardware, Streaming, Computer Vision, Cloud Infrastructure, Security, Manufacturing, and Product. You will also work with Verkada Linux, the shared OS layer across all Verkada product lines, to incubate platform capabilities on cameras and contribute them back for use across the company product lines.
This role combines deep technical leadership with people management. We are committed to a thriving in-office culture, and this role requires onsite presence at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.
What You'll Do
Lead the team
Lead and grow a team of storage, firmware, and systems engineers, and recruit and retain top-tier embedded talent as the team expands its charter.
Mentor engineers through design reviews, code reviews, career development, and execution management.
Define the technical vision and multi-quarter roadmap for camera storage and firmware platform, balancing fleet-wide investments against support for new camera launches.
Establish engineering best practices around testing, observability, incident response, root-cause analysis, and long-term maintainability.
Drive storage optimizations
Storage stack and architecture: Own the on-camera storage stack end to end, including filesystems (ext4, UBIFS), video layout and indexing, SD/eMMC drivers, and raw NAND. Lead next-generation storage architecture such as new SD card modes, partition-level encryption, and secure deletion of expired footage.
Reliability, endurance, and retention: Guarantee footage integrity through power loss, filesystem corruption, and failing media. Minimize write amplification with aligned, batched writes, and extend retention through index compression, smarter SD card capacity allocation, and better high versus low-quality stream storage.
Storage observability: Build deep storage observability of SD and NAND health, erase counts, bad blocks, UBI counters, writes per hour, and retention metrics that feed release go/no-go decisions.
Testing: Build hardware-in-the-loop testing for storage disaster cases such as full-period retention, OTA transitions across storage layout changes, partition reformats, EEPROM recovery, and SD controller firmware updates.
Media qualification: Partner with Hardware teams and external flash vendors to evaluate, qualify, and validate next-generation storage media.
Backend and network storage: Guide the evolution of storage-adjacent backend systems for retention, cloud backup, archives, and storage health notifications. Build on-premises storage appliances where cameras back up footage to RAID-backed hard drives over the LAN, with SMART-based drive health monitoring.
Drive firmware platform improvements
Boot and shutdown: Optimize boot and shutdown paths across the boot stack, kernel, userspace services, and backend connection. This is critical for reducing downtime and maximizing video footage retention.
System resources: Optimize memory, power, and network on resource-constrained embedded devices. Reduce DRAM and flash footprint of firmware services. Prevent brownouts at peak load with power management schemes such as Dynamic Frequency Scaling (DFS). Make network traffic between device and backend more efficient and resilient with techniques such as retry backoff with jitter and connection consolidation.
Device State Management: Orchestrate device-level state transitions such as system and service restarts, OTA, DSP pipeline restart, commissioning and decommissioning. Sequencing these operations in the correct order is critical for correct device function.
Observability and debuggability: Add core dumps and stack traces for crashes, reliable IPC message delivery, power-on self tests, standardized per-service and fleet-wide metrics, and system-wide log levels.
Developer and release velocity: Improve build and kernel tooling, remote serial and flashing access, AI-assisted code review and workflows, and standardized manufacturing release and flashing automation across camera models.
Operate at fleet scale
Own fleet-wide reliability metrics for retention, storage health, crash rates, memory pressure, boot time, and power, and make them visible in release go/no-go decisions.
Find and fix issues before customers notice them, using diagnostic data from across the fleet.

BS/MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
8+ years of software engineering experience in embedded or systems software, including 2+ years leading or managing high-performing systems, storage, platform, or infrastructure teams.
Experience designing storage systems for continuous, high-throughput write workloads, such as video recording.
Strong expertise in systems programming in C/C++; experience with Go or other higher-level languages preferred.
Hands-on experience profiling and optimizing system-level performance, memory, and power on resource-constrained devices.
Experience designing concurrent userspace services and IPC mechanisms (shared memory, sockets, message queues) and reasoning about their trade-offs.
Experience debugging complex OS or storage issues in production, across large deployed fleets.
Demonstrated success driving technical strategy and aligning multiple teams around shared platform investments.

BS/MS in Computer Science (or similar degree).

Strong familiarity with low-level systems topics, including file system layout, memory management, the Yocto build system, device drivers, kernel debugging, eBPF, and the MMC protocol.

Model Evaluation: Lead detection evaluation, model consistency, and ongoing quality improvements for various CV and ML pipelines.

Service Ownership: Accountable for a portfolio of production services including submission endpoints, inference pipelines, APIs and database layer.
Migrations & Deprecations: Execute in-flight migrations into new advanced pipelines and deprecations of old pipelines without disrupting customer-facing features.
Scalability & Performance: Drive large-org optimizations, inference engine stability, gRPC load balancing, and connection-hardening work to keep the pipeline healthy as the fleet grows.

On-Call & Incident Response: Own the team on-call rotation, post-mortem quality, and the new programs required to scale the team.
Test Coverage: Expand integration test coverage and search pipeline change testing to catch regressions before they reach production.
Telemetry & Dashboards: Define and track the metrics that matter (e.g. API latency, search quality, inference stability, field reliability, etc.) via dashboards and service SLOs.

7+ years of software engineering experience, including 2+ years managing backend or ML engineering teams.
Track record leading 5+ engineers running production services at meaningful scale.

Deep proficiency in Python plus Go/Java/C++; fluent in distributed systems (gRPC, Kafka) and a major cloud provider (AWS preferred). Hands-on with at least one production vector database or search engine (OpenSearch, Turbopuffer, FAISS, Milvus, pgvector, etc.).
Strong operational instincts: on-call ownership, post-mortem rigor, and a habit of defining metrics and building evals to drive quality on high-availability services.

Build reconciliation and controls that let Finance close the books daily and let auditors trace any recognized dollar back to its source — with the auditability, immutability, and lineage a maturing company requires.
Partner with Finance, Accounting, Revenue, and Product to turn revenue-recognition policy (ASC 606, deferred revenue, contract modifications, true-ups) into precise, testable system behavior.
Lead major features end-to-end and bring others along — through design reviews, code reviews, crisp written docs, and direct mentorship.

Help shape the platform's roadmap toward the company's biggest long-term bets as Verkada scales and matures.

8+ years building backend services with strong correctness, consistency, and durability guarantees at scale.
Depth in financial or transactional systems: ledgers, double-entry accounting, billing, payments, or revenue recognition — you understand why idempotency, exactly-once semantics, immutability, and reconciliation matter, and you've built for them.
Comfort working shoulder-to-shoulder with Finance and Accounting — or a track record of getting deep in an unfamiliar, high-stakes domain fast.

We are looking for a founding Staff Engineer to lead the technical architecture of our next-generation Spatial Platform. For the past decade, floor plans have been static images; we are rebuilding that foundation from the ground up as a high-performance, interactive, and collaborative 3D engine.
This is a greenfield role for a builder who wants to own a core pillar of Verkada’s infrastructure before we hit the public markets. You won't just build features—you will architect a platform that supports 8+ product lines, solving the "hard math" of geospatial projections and the "hard graphics" of rendering thousands of interactive assets at a buttery-smooth 60 FPS.

Build the Rendering Platform: Design a high-performance rendering architecture that supports both an interactive viewer for high-density geospatial visualization and a precision editing surface for real-time vertex manipulation.
Set the UX Bar: Partner with Design to define the interaction model for spatial editing — easing curves, snapping behavior, cursor states, loading transitions — and hold the line on pixel-level polish across the platform.
Optimize for Latency: Solve the "500-element wall" with partial GPU buffer updates and custom shaders, ensuring sub-millisecond input latency during real-time vertex manipulation.
Spatial Intelligence: Develop power-user tools like real-time 3D line-of-sight analysis, signal strength heatmaps, and AI-driven hardware placement suggestions.
Build the Sync Engine: Own the client-side CRDT architecture (Yjs/Automerge-class) powering offline-first, multi-user editing — document model, local persistence, presence, and conflict resolution.

Eye for Detail: Pixel-perfect execution — you notice the half-pixel misalignment, the 16ms jank, the easing curve that feels "off." You hold a high bar for visual polish and won't ship until interactions feel right.
Product Grit: Ability to bridge the gap between CAD-level precision and consumer-grade UX, partnering closely with Design to turn rough specs into delightful, production-grade experiences.
Mathematical Precision: Understanding of coordinate system conversions, geospatial projections, and 3D geometry.

Graphics Stack: Experience with Deck.gl, MapLibre, Three.js, or raw WebGL/WebGPU.
Collaborative Systems: Experience with real-time sync architectures (e.g., Yjs, Automerge, or Operational Transforms).

Own It, End to End: Take full ownership of customer issues from "we have a problem" to "problem solved"
Team Up with Tech Leaders: Partner directly with Engineering and Product teams to test new gear and hunt down bugs before anyone else
Share Knowledge: Write Knowledge Base content that helps thousands of users
What You Bring
Available for a full-time (40 hours per week) in-person internship for Spring 2027 in San Mateo, CA
A third or fourth-year student in a Bachelor's degree program from an accredited university, with a focus on a related technical field like Networking, Telecommunications, Systems Administration, Information Technology, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Cybersecurity

You're a problem-solver with a keen eye for detail
You can clearly and confidently communicate complex technical information
You thrive in a team environment
Industry certifications (like CCNP, CCNA, or Network+) are a bonus, but not required!

At Verkada, we believe that internships should be as rewarding, supportive, and fun as they are impactful! That’s why we’re committed to providing a world-class experience that supports both your personal well-being and professional growth. Here are just a few of the perks and benefits you can expect as a Verkada Technical Support Engineering intern:
Monthly housing stipend for those relocating to the area, in addition to a competitive hourly wage
Daily lunch catered onsite, complimentary barista-made drinks, and fully stocked snacks to keep you fueled
Intern-exclusive events and mixers, allowing you to connect with other interns across different teams
Cross-functional collaboration opportunities, giving you real exposure to how teams work together
Meetings with company executives so you can hear directly from leaders and gain insight into building a successful career
333 program: you can go out with your fellow interns after work and expense $30 off a meal
Friendly tournaments involving Super Smash Bros, Magic, and other games
Intern exclusive bingo cards that allow you to explore the Bay Area and win fun swag!
And more! From team-building activities to mentorship opportunities, we’re here to support your growth every step of the way
Don't just take it from us, hear directly from some of our current and past interns on their experience:
“A benefit of being a TSE at Verkada is about being a part of a fast-growing company. You learn about the latest products deeply and learn how to effectively communicate what you have learned in an easy-to-understand way for customers: ‘If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it well enough.’ Albert Einstein” - Daniel, TSE Intern, London
“After training (which feels a lot like university lectures) you spend time in queue, which is basically being on-call for the next chat/call/email that comes in. When a customer needs something, whether that’s information about a product, how to set up that product, or that product having a bit of a moment, you are the one who gets to be the source of truth for that person. Being able to communicate this to them in a reasonable amount of time is paramount to doing well in this role” - Tedrick, TSE Intern, HQ
“This internship has given me a lot to think about in terms of career goals. I would say in particular this internship is a great way to build your connections for the Silicon Valley area if your goal is to work in the Tech space. It’s also given me a unique perspective and understanding of enterprise equipment. It serves as a great launching point for your career.” - Thomas, TSE Intern, HQ
